The paper does not establish the algebra or ordering used to form unified multimodal tokens from text, sequence, and structure representations.
The paper does not document the internal encoding path for small-molecule structures or the exact candidate-domain decomposition used in drug-domain retrieval.
The paper names PROCYON-BIND as a PDBBind-fine-tuned configuration, but the atlas seed lists only PROCYON and PROCYON-SPLIT.
Exact prompt templates, special tokens, attention masks, causal-label construction, and sampling distributions are unspecified.
The paper does not specify how protein libraries, domain libraries, or peptide candidates are represented before ranking.

The paper does not document a distinct input path for every downstream application; application-specific trajectories therefore reuse the documented PROCYON architecture only where the source explicitly supports that reuse.

evidence.quote: In protein retrieval, PROCYON retrieves a ranked list of proteins that match a user's prompt. First, the protein language model processes protein sequences and projects them into the unified latent space via a retrieval-specific projector. The natural language prompt is then processed by the LLM and projected into the unified latent space by a query connector, allowing PROCYON to identify the proteins most closely related to the projected prompt (Supplementary Note 1, Extended Data Figure 1).

PROCYON is a multimodal protein foundation model with 11 billion parameters. Composed of a Llama-3-8B language model [31] and encoders for protein sequence (ESM-2 3B [32]) and structure (GearNet [19]), PROCYON can process inputs of natural language and protein sequence and structure. To support a wide range of downstream tasks, PROCYON has two output modes: protein retrieval and phenotype generation (Figure 1b).
